plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if you win; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my value of $42.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. This holds regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies, since your bid only affects whether you win, not what you pay if you win. Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $29.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks losses on ties/overpayment and underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $48, I should bid exactly $48 to guarantee optimal outcomes - winning whenever profitable and never overpaying.
